title: What the Ground Remembers
objective: After this level you can explain what archaeology shows about Rome’s earliest villages.
summary: Latin farmers built huts on the Palatine by about the 8th century BCE. Hilltop villages merged, and the marshy Forum valley was drained.

cards.headline: Forget the wolf for a moment. What does the ground say?
cards.body: Under the ruins on Rome’s Palatine Hill lie traces of the city’s first huts. They tell a quieter story than twins and a she-wolf.

cards.headline: Huts on a hill
cards.body: The first Romans were Latins, a people of the region of Latium in central Italy. On the Palatine Hill, archaeologists have found traces of their Iron Age huts from around the 8th century BCE. Now hold that next to the traditional founding date, 753 BCE. The huts sit close to the traditional founding: the shovel and the storytellers land in the same century. Not bad for a tale with a wolf in it.

cards.headline: From villages to a town
cards.body: Early Rome wasn’t one city. It was a cluster of small hilltop villages that gradually merged into one community. Down between the hills lay a marshy valley. It was drained, and that soggy low ground became the Roman Forum, the center of Roman public life. Before it was famous, it was a bog.

cards.context: The Cloaca Maxima, Rome’s great drain, helped dry out that marshy Forum valley. Parts of it still carry water today. Somewhere under the modern city, a very old drain is still doing its job.

cards.headline: Early Rome: excavated
learned: Huts on the Palatine date to about the 8th century BCE
Hilltop villages merged into a town
The drained valley became the Forum

questions.prompt: What have archaeologists found on the Palatine Hill?

options.label: A stone list of the seven kings
Remains of a Greek colony
options.rationale: Rome was not a Greek colony.

questions.explanation: Hut remains from around the 8th century BCE show where early Romans lived.

questions.prompt: How did the Roman Forum come to exist?

options.label: A marshy valley was drained and became Rome's public center
It was carved into the top of a hill
options.rationale: It lies in a valley between hills.

options.label: It was dug out as a stone quarry
It began as a harbor on the sea

questions.explanation: The low, marshy ground between the hills was drained, helped by the Cloaca Maxima, and became the Forum.

questions.prompt: From Level 1: how does the date of the Palatine huts compare with Rome’s traditional founding?

options.label: They are a thousand years older
They date close to the traditional founding
They date from the time of the emperors

questions.explanation: Huts from around the 8th century BCE sit close to the traditional date of 753 BCE.
